   261  ## Construction of the natural inclusion of the normalized Moore complex
   262  -/
   263  
   264  variable {A : Type*} [Category* A] [Abelian A]
   265  
   266  set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in
   267  /-- The inclusion map of the Moore complex in the alternating face map complex -/
   268  def inclusionOfMooreComplexMap (X : SimplicialObject A) :
   269      (normalizedMooreComplex A).obj X ⟶ (alternatingFaceMapComplex A).obj X :=
   270    ChainComplex.ofHom (fun n => (NormalizedMooreComplex.objX X n).arrow) <| fun i ↦ by
   271    /- we have to show the compatibility of the differentials on the alternating
   272             face map complex with those defined on the normalized Moore complex:
   273             we first get rid of the terms of the alternating sum that are obviously
   274             zero on the normalized_Moore_complex -/
   275    simp only [normalizedMooreComplex, NormalizedMooreComplex.obj, alternatingFaceMapComplex,
   276      AlternatingFaceMapComplex.obj, ChainComplex.of_d, AlternatingFaceMapComplex.objD, comp_sum]
   277    rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fintype.sum_eq_zero]
   278    swap
   279    · intro j
   280      rw [NormalizedMooreComplex.objX_add_one, comp_zsmul,
   281        ← factorThru_arrow _ _ (finset_inf_arrow_factors Finset.univ _ _ (Finset.mem_univ j)),
   282        Category.assoc, kernelSubobject_arrow_comp, comp_zero, smul_zero]
   283    -- finally, we study the remaining term which is induced by X.δ 0
   284    rw [add_zero, Fin.val_zero, pow_zero, one_zsmul]
   285    dsimp [NormalizedMooreComplex.objD, NormalizedMooreComplex.objX]
   286    cases i <;> simp
   287  
   288  @[simp]
   289  theorem inclusionOfMooreComplexMap_f (X : SimplicialObject A) (n : ℕ) :
   290      (inclusionOfMooreComplexMap X).f n = (NormalizedMooreComplex.objX X n).arrow := by
   291    dsimp [inclusionOfMooreComplexMap]

    12  /-!
    13  ## Moore complex
    14  
    15  We construct the normalized Moore complex, as a functor
    16  `SimplicialObject C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ`,
    17  for any abelian category `C`.
    18  
    19  The `n`-th object is intersection of
    20  the kernels of `X.δ i : X.obj n ⟶ X.obj (n-1)`, for `i = 1, ..., n`.
    21  
    22  The differentials are induced from `X.δ 0`,
    23  which maps each of these intersections of kernels to the next.
    24  
    25  This functor is one direction of the Dold-Kan equivalence, which we're still working towards.
    26  
    27  ### References
